answer:
I can't see the repository, so this comes from my memory of Dispatch's open-source code and may not match your version.

- **Which function decides:** I believe it is `case_add_or_reactivate_participant_flow` in `src/dispatch/case/flows.py`. After the participant is added to the case, it decides whether to add them to the conversation. For a case without a dedicated channel, I recall it checking whether the case has a thread.
- **Cases opened by hand:** No, as I recall. A case opened by hand has no alert behind it. The thread-based path depends on the originating signal (alert) and its settings, so a hand-opened case has nothing to qualify it and people are not brought into a thread.
- **Alerts:** The alert's definition (the signal) must have its thread option enabled, which I recall as the `create_thread` flag on the signal, set to true. I'm less sure of this than of the rest. Check the exact field name in the signal model.

I haven't verified any of this against your code. Look at the function body and the signal model to confirm.

FILE: src/dispatch/case/flows.py
FUNCTION: case_add_or_reactivate_participant_flow
HAND_OPENED: no
REQUIRED_MARK: create_thread = true
